Write a sheet for people to label

Source: R/doc-labels.R
gr_label_sheet.Rd

Writes a CSV with one row per item, an item_id column, the columns a person needs to judge the item, and empty columns for their decisions, with a short instructions file beside it. Read the filled sheet back with gr_read_labels().

Usage

gr_label_sheet(
  kind = c("qa", "screening", "extraction", "calibration", "judge"),
  items,
  path = NULL,
  blind = TRUE,
  reviewers = 1,
  fields = NULL
)

Arguments

kind

"qa", "screening", "extraction", "calibration" or "judge"; see "Kinds of sheet".

items

A data frame with one row per item. Its ids come from an item_id column, else an id column; without either they are made from the kind and the row number ("qa-0001"), so pass the same rows in the same order to gr_read_labels(). Column names are matched exactly: a column such as ideal_answer is never taken for id, so reference answers cannot reach a blind sheet as ids.

path

Where to write the CSV. NULL returns the sheet without writing. The instructions go to <name>_instructions.txt beside it.

blind

Leave model output out of the sheet; see "Blind sheets".

reviewers

How many people label each item, a whole number of at least 1; see "Several reviewers".

fields

For kind = "extraction", the fields: names, a gr_fields() schema or a gr_protocol(). A schema's descriptions and allowed values go into the instructions.

Value

The sheet as a data frame (several reviewers' sheets stacked, with their reviewer column), invisibly when written; then its paths attribute holds the files written.

Kinds of sheet

"qa"

Questions about documents. Items need document and question. The person fills answerable (yes or no: is the answer in the document), answer (required when answerable) and quote (the passage that gives it).

"screening"

Records to judge for eligibility. Items need document; title, authors, year, journal and abstract are copied when present. The person fills human_decision (include or exclude) and human_note, the columns gr_calibrate() reads.

"extraction"

Documents to extract fields from. Items need document, one row per document, and fields names the fields. The person fills one column per field, writing "not reported" when the document does not report it.

"calibration"

The graded set a signal is calibrated on. Items need document and question, and must include questions the document cannot answer. The person fills answerable and answer, and on a sheet with blind = FALSE, correct (yes or no: is the model's answer, shown beside it, right).

"judge"

Candidates a judge scores, to validate the judge against. Items need candidate, the text being judged, and may give question or criterion. The person fills verdict (pass or fail).

Every sheet also has a free-text note column (human_note for screening).

Blind sheets

With blind = TRUE only the columns listed above for the kind are copied from items; nothing else is, so no model output, score, verdict or sampling detail reaches the sheet by accident. With blind = FALSE the other columns are copied too, each named model_<name> unless it already starts with model_. Columns about how items were sampled or assigned (cluster, split, stratum, strata, inclusion_prob, weight, frame_n, screened_n, sampled_from) are never written, except on a screening sheet. There a blind sheet carries the frame as the opaque key a blind gr_reference() sheet carries, made from plain frame names when items has them (a stacked frame also needs stratum, inclusion_prob, frame_n and screened_n), so the sheet read back without items still tells gr_calibrate() what was sampled; with blind = FALSE the columns are written as they are. Give the same items to gr_read_labels() to join the rest back.

Calibration grading needs the model's answer, so a blind calibration sheet has no correct column: the person records the reference answer, and the model's answers are scored against it afterwards.

Several reviewers

With reviewers = k above 1, each reviewer gets a sheet of their own, <name>_r1.csv to <name>_r<k>.csv, with a reviewer column already filled, so that no reviewer sees another's decisions. gr_read_labels() reads them together.

How many items each set needs

These are the sizes harnessr's development plan budgets for its own evaluation, given here as a starting point, not as rules.

QA

About 480 questions over 88 documents, plus 88 explanatory questions, labelled by two people and adjudicated, with quotes. At an intraclass correlation of 0.2 for the paired difference between two settings within a document, this supports about an 8 point margin before a Holm correction; a contrast that sets a default needs about 136 scored documents, or a margin of about 10.5 points.

Screening reference

7 to 9 reviews, about 200 eligible and 1,800 ineligible records, with two blind reviewers on one recent review. See gr_screen_sample_size() for the sample a recall target needs.

Extraction

60 documents by 10 fields, two people, with Krippendorff's alpha per field at its level of measurement (gr_extract_agreement()).

Calibration graded set

Sized from the error count it needs, not from the QA set: n >= 100 / (1 - accuracy) items, so that about 100 are wrong, with accuracy from a pilot. At 85% accuracy that is about 670 items, on top of the QA set; at 80-90% accuracy the 480 QA questions hold only about 48 to 96 errors.

Judge validation

100 to 200 blind labels with at least 50 positive and 50 negative items, plus 50 labelled by two people for the agreement between them. A bare total is not enough: at 10% prevalence 100 labels hold 10 positives.

The default shares of hr_assign_splits() put 10% of documents in dev, 10% in exploratory, 30% in calibration and 50% in test.

The file

The CSV is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, as gr_reference() writes it, so a spreadsheet opens accented text correctly; save it back as "CSV UTF-8". Leave a decision empty only for an item not yet labelled.

See also

gr_read_labels(), hr_assign_splits(), gr_reference()

Other reference sets: gr_read_labels(), hr_assign_splits()

Examples

qa <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "a.pdf", "b.pdf"),
                 question = c("What was revenue?", "Who audited it?",
                              "When did the trial start?"),
                 model_answer = c("45.2 million", "Not stated", "2019"))
gr_label_sheet("qa", qa)
#>   item_id document                  question answerable answer quote note
#> 1 qa-0001    a.pdf         What was revenue?       <NA>   <NA>  <NA> <NA>
#> 2 qa-0002    a.pdf           Who audited it?       <NA>   <NA>  <NA> <NA>
#> 3 qa-0003    b.pdf When did the trial start?       <NA>   <NA>  <NA> <NA>

path <- file.path(tempdir(), "qa-labels.csv")
gr_label_sheet("qa", qa, path = path)
#> Wrote 3 item(s) to '/tmp/Rtmp0cYkSI/qa-labels.csv', with instructions in '/tmp/Rtmp0cYkSI/qa-labels_instructions.txt'. Read the filled sheet back with gr_read_labels().
readLines(sub("[.]csv$", "_instructions.txt", path))
#>  [1] "Labelling instructions: qa sheet"                                             
#>  [2] ""                                                                             
#>  [3] "Each row is a question about one document. Read the document and fill in:"    
#>  [4] "  answerable  yes or no: does the document answer the question?"              
#>  [5] "  answer      the answer, in your own words (required when answerable is yes)"
#>  [6] "  quote       the passage of the document that gives the answer"              
#>  [7] ""                                                                             
#>  [8] "Use the `note` column for anything worth recording about a row."              
#>  [9] "Leave a row's decisions empty only if you have not labelled it yet."          
#> [10] "Do not change, add or delete `item_id` values or rows."                       
#> [11] "The sheet is blind: it does not show what the model said. Do not look it up." 
#> [12] ""                                                                             
#> [13] "Save the file as CSV UTF-8, keeping its name and columns."                    
#> [14] "Read it back in R with gr_read_labels()."
